I'm 50 this year and I've been farming these 8 mu in Quzhou since I was a teenager. I finished middle school, so I can read the extension pamphlets, but honestly I trust what I see with my own eyes more than what's on paper. Last year my wheat did about 480 jin per mu, and the maize after it did around 520 jin. Not a great year — the spring was dry — but not terrible either. This year I'm sticking with what I know: wheat in October, then maize right after the wheat comes off in June. That's what my neighbors do, and it's insurance. If one crop has a bad year, the other usually pulls through.

For the wheat, I'll use an improved variety — probably Jimai 22 or something similar from the seed shop. I know the extension guy said 15 kg of nitrogen per mu is enough, but I've always put down a bit more, around 16 kg, because I'd rather waste a little money on fertilizer than risk a big yield drop. I use rotary tillage before sowing — my neighbor has a machine and I pay him about 50 yuan per mu. For maize, there's no time to till after wheat harvest. The window is maybe five days, so I'll plant directly into the stubble with a no-till planter. Denghai 605 is what everyone plants now; it's hybrid seed and costs more, but it yields better and the cooperative always buys it.

Irrigation is expensive — electricity for the well pump keeps going up — but you can't skip it. Wheat needs three times: once before winter to help it survive the cold, once at jointing in spring, and once at grain filling. Maize needs two, at silking and filling. Any more and I'm just throwing money away. For chemicals, I spray herbicide once on each crop and insecticide twice. The corn borer was bad two years ago so I don't take chances with maize, and the aphids always come for the wheat in spring.

I thought about planting some cotton like Old Wang down the road, but cotton needs too much hand labor for picking and pruning, and my back isn't what it used to be. Wheat and maize can be harvested by machine, and I can sell both easily at the village collection point. So that's my plan — 8 mu of wheat-maize double crop, same as last year, same as the year before. If it ain't broke, don't fix it.
